summary: Observation of a luminous white sphere in the NE sky: astronomical mistake with the planet Jupiter.
description: On November 3, 1953, at 7:14 PM UTC (8:14 PM local time), the press reported several sightings of a luminous white sphere in the sky. This phenomenon was stationary in the northeast under a mostly clear sky. A controller recorded his observation in the tower's logbook on November 3, 1953. He filed a report on November 20, 1953, indicating that two other military personnel had also made the same observation. A star chart showed Jupiter in the northeast with a high magnitude (-2.22) and an elevation of 3.6°. GEIPAN classified this case as A: astronomical misidentification of the planet Jupiter.

summary: Observations of the round trip of a red-orange luminous phenomenon in the sky: strange unidentified phenomenon.
description: On April 11, 1953, at 9:10 PM, three witnesses at an Air Force depot observed the silent movement of a large red-orange dot. The captain described a phenomenon making a round trip across 45 arcseconds of the celestial vault in 6 minutes, following an irregular broken line forming angles of 15 arcseconds around the axis of movement. The 180 arcsecond turn was also achieved through successive changes of heading. These changes of heading occurred every second. The two other witnesses followed the phenomenon for two to three minutes. The phenomenon was eventually lost from sight. Only one witness statement was recorded. This phenomenon did not resemble any of the known misinterpretations. GEIPAN classified this case as D1: unidentified strange phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a fixed bright orange point in the sky then movement and disappearance due to a decrease in intensity: lack of information.
description: On March 20, 1959, at approximately 8:15 PM, two witnesses in Timbuktu, Mali, observed a low, bright orange point of light on the horizon. The point appeared to move rather slowly from northeast to southwest without leaving a trail. It moved away and decreased in size and intensity before disappearing completely. Only one witness account was recorded. An astronomical survey revealed no celestial bodies in the indicated direction. Furthermore, the object appeared to be in motion. The phenomenon as described could correspond to an aircraft in the distance, seen head-on with its landing lights on. GEIPAN classified this case as Category C due to a lack of information and corroboration.
